jsonld.description: The full English sealed in pastry to go: a proper shortcrust pasty crimped around sausage, bacon, beans, and a whole quail egg or a cube of set egg custard, baked until the crust is golden and the filling steams at the first break. The pasty is Cornwall's gift to the portable lunch applied to the portable breakfast — the components cooked ahead, wrapped raw-side in pastry, and finished together in the oven so the filling arrives juicy and the crust arrives flaky. skeleton:
Sausage-and-Bean Breakfast Pasties

British · Medium · Makes 6 pasties

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English sealed in pastry to go: a proper shortcrust pasty crimped around sausage, bacon, beans, and a whole quail egg or a cube of set egg custard, baked until the crust is golden and the filling steams at the first break. The pasty is Cornwall's gift to the portable lunch applied to the portable breakfast — the components cooked ahead, wrapped raw-side in pastry, and finished together in the oven so the filling arrives juicy and the crust arrives flaky. The technique is pasty discipline: the pastry must be strong enough to crimp and hold a wet-ish filling (a hot-water pastry or a firm shortcrust, not a delicate one), the filling must be pre-cooked and cooled (raw sausage floods the crust), and the egg — the full English's soul — must be solved for the sealed format: a quail egg cracked in raw cooks perfectly in the pastry's 25 minutes, or a cube of just-set egg custard holds its slice.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The pastry

The filling (cook and cool first)

For assembly and bake

- **Cook and cool the filling completely** — 20 minutes at least. Warm filling softens the pastry's fat as you crimp, and the seal fails in the oven's first ten minutes. - **The pastry's rest is structural:** 30 minutes chilled after mixing relaxes the gluten so the crust rolls without springing back and crimps without cracking. - **The egg decision:** quail eggs cracked raw into each pasty bake to perfect jammy in 25 minutes — the simpler and better route. The set-omelette cube guarantees neat slices but loses the run. Choose run.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Pastry: firm, rested, rolled even at 3 mm; strong enough to crimp.
  • Filling: cooked, cooled, cohesive — no free liquid anywhere.
  • Seal: continuous crimp, one vent, glaze unbroken.
  • Bake: deep gold, no splits, 10 minutes' rest before the first break.

Sausage-and-Bean Breakfast Pasties

Prep: 40 minutes, plus 30 minutes dough rest · Cook: 30 minutes · Total: About 1 hour 40 minutes · Makes 6 pasties

Ingredients

The pastry

  • 300 g plain flour
  • 120 g cold butter, cubed, plus 30 g lard or extra butter (lard makes the authentic crisp; all-butter is the gentler option)
  • 1 tsp (5 g) fine sea salt
  • About 100 ml ice-cold water

The filling (cook and cool first)

  • 3 pork sausages (240 g), skins removed, crumbled and browned
  • 3 rashers (150 g) back bacon, chopped and cooked
  • 150 g baked beans, drained of their loose sauce (a thick bean holds; a wet one floods) and lightly crushed
  • 1 small onion (100 g), finely diced and sweated soft
  • 30 g mature Cheddar, grated
  • 2 g salt, 1 g pepper, 1 g chopped thyme
  • 6 quail eggs (90 g), or 3 hen eggs beaten with a pinch of salt and set in a warm pan as a thin omelette, cut into 6

For assembly and bake

  • 1 large egg (55 g), beaten, for glazing
  • Flour, for rolling

Instructions

  1. **Make and rest the pastry.** Rub the butter and lard into the flour and salt to breadcrumbs, add just enough ice water to bring it together into a firm dough, wrap, and chill 30 minutes. Checkpoint — a firm, pliable dough that rolls without cracking at the edges — test a small ball; it should flatten to a thin disc without splitting.
  2. **Cook and cool the filling.** Brown the crumbled sausagemeat 6 minutes, add the bacon for 3, and the onion alongside until soft. Off the heat, fold in the drained, lightly crushed beans, the Cheddar, salt, pepper, and thyme. Spread on a plate and cool 20 minutes. Checkpoint — the filling is cohesive — it mounds on a spoon — with no free liquid pooling on the plate. Wet beans get another minute over heat to thicken; loose filling is the pasty's one fatal flaw.
  3. **Roll and fill.** Divide the dough into 6 and roll each piece to a 16 cm circle, 3 mm thick. Divide the filling down the centres, leaving a 2.5 cm border all round. Make a small well in each filling and crack in a quail egg (or lay the omelette cube). Checkpoint — each circle is even-thickness with a clear border, the filling in a compact central log, and the quail egg sitting in its well — visible, intact, waiting.
  4. **Fold, crimp, glaze.** Fold each circle over into a half-moon (or the D-shape, the Cornish way), press the edges together, and crimp: fold and roll the edge over itself in sequence, working along the seal — or press firm with a fork, the honest alternative. Glaze all over with the beaten egg, and cut one small steam vent in each. Checkpoint — each pasty is sealed along its whole edge with no cracks or gaps, the crimp (or fork-press) continuous, the glaze unbroken, and the vent — a 5 mm slit — the only opening. Lift each pasty and check its underside: no thin spots, no filling showing.
  5. **Bake — 25–30 minutes at 200 °C.** Egg-glazed, vented, and baked on a floured tray 25–30 minutes until deep gold and blistered, the vents steaming gently by the end. Checkpoint — deep golden crust with darker blisters at the crimp, no split seams, and a pasty that feels firm-but-springy when pressed at its belly. Rest 10 minutes before eating — the steam inside is scalding and the rest finishes the egg.

Finish & Plate

Eaten hot in the hand, from the vent's end first — the steam's release, then the egg's run, then the filling — with brown sauce for the crust's edge. Cold, they are the lunchbox and picnic standard, the egg set to slice rather than run. A batch of six feeds a breakfast table once or a household's week of mornings.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Seams split in the ovenWet filling, warm filling at crimp, or no ventDrain and cool the filling; the steam vent
Soggy undersideThin base or cool tray3 mm even rolling; the tray preheated or a hot baking stone
Filling dryLean sausagemeat or over-drained beansKeep the beans' crush moist; a 70/30 sausage
Crimp cracked on rollingPastry too dry or under-restedThe full 30-minute rest; a sprinkle more water next batch

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **The batch-cooker's prize:** baked pasties keep 3 days refrigerated and freeze 3 months (reheat from frozen, 35 minutes at 180 °C, foil over the crimp). Unbaked, assembled pasties freeze equally well — bake from frozen with 10 extra minutes. - **Variation — the black pudding pasty:** 100 g black pudding dice replacing the bacon — the West Country's darker breakfast parcel. - **Variation — the vegetarian pasty:** the vegetarian master's beans with mushrooms and Cheddar, the quail egg kept — the meatless traveller. - **The format trilogy completed:** pie (custard-set), pizza (flat and fast), pasty (sealed, portable) — the full English's three baked forms, each with its own water discipline and its own moment of glory.

The pasty's interior steams in its own chamber — which is why the filling must start cooked and the quail egg works so well: the chamber is a perfect 25-minute egg environment, hotter than a pan and gentler than an oven's dry air. The Cornish miners' wife who worked this out deserves the credit history forgot to give her.

methodSteps.chefsNote: the bean-draining is the filling's one quiet trick and it deserves a sentence of explanation: tinned beans carry a loose sauce that is mostly sweetened water, and inside a sealed pastry chamber that water turns to steam with nowhere to go — the crust soaks from within and the crimp gives way. Draining the loose sauce and lightly crushing the beans turns them into their own binder, holding their moisture as texture rather than releasing it as steam. The flavour lost to the drain is replaced by the Cheddar and the pan's fond — a trade the pasty has been making since long before anyone wrote it down.
